QF.id: III-C Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices_11

question.text: As discussed in Case 8.2 (the Supreme Court order on front-running), trading ahead of customer orders by an intermediary was recognized under which regulation of the PFUTP Regulations?

explanation.text: The Logic: As discussed in Case 8.2 (the Supreme Court order), trading ahead by an intermediary has been recognized under regulation 4(2)(q) of the PFUTP Regulations, 2003. The Trap: While front-running can also be examined under the general fraud provisions of Regulation 3, the specific recognition relied on in Case 8.2 is under Regulation 4(2)(q). Note: Non-intermediary front running (such as tippee trading) can separately be brought under Regulations 3 and 4(1) as a fraudulent or unfair trade practice.
